label: AF3 code + AF3 native weights
notes: Reference arm. Same container as af3_openbind.json — the AlphaFold3 fork at
juliabuhmann/alphafold3 @ 1fff5c4 — so the CODE is identical between the two arms
and any difference is attributable to the weights alone.
model_dir holds af3.bin.zst, the DeepMind-issued AlphaFold3 parameters, which you
must request separately (see WEIGHTS_TERMS_OF_USE in the AlphaFold 3 repo).
$HOME and a leading ~ are expanded by run_workflow.sh. --of3_weights is off, so
run_alphafold.py takes its stock parameter-loading path.
engine/weights/use_templates are the three axes the comparison varies. They are
read by run_workflow.sh to pick the input JSONs and the launcher, and this file is
copied to predictions/<name_tag>/config.json so stages 04 and 05 can label every
output row with the arm that produced it.
use_templates is the arm's template switch. AlphaFold3 has NO inference-time
template flag — the complete flag list in run_alphafold.py offers only
--max_template_date, which feeds the data pipeline we are not running — so with
--norun_data_pipeline templates reach the model only through the input JSON.
slurm/predict.sbatch therefore applies the switch itself: with use_templates=false
it writes a copy of the JSON with `templates: []` (AlphaFold3's own 'use no
templates' value) into node-local scratch for that task. work/af3_input/ always
holds the templates-ON superset and is never forked per arm.
num_recycles=3 rather than AlphaFold3's default of 10: it is what the earlier
pooled-PPI benchmarks pinned, and both arms here use the same value, so the
comparison is like-for-like. It does make absolute DockQ here lower than a
stock-default AF3 run would give — see README, 'Limitations'.
